import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 224

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/224](https://www.erdosproblems.com/224)
- [DaGr62] Danzer, L. and Gr\"{u}nbaum, B., *\"{U}ber zwei Probleme
  bez\"{u}glich konvexer K\"{o}rper von P. Erd\H{o}s und von V. L. Klee*.
  Math. Z. (1962), 95-99.
-/

namespace Erdos224

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- The angle $yxz$ is obtuse. -/
def ObtuseAt {d : ℕ} (x y z : ℝ^d) : Prop :=
  inner ℝ (y - x) (z - x) < 0

/--
If $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is any set of $2^d+1$ points then some three points in $A$ determine an obtuse angle.

The general case was proved by Danzer and Gr\"{u}nbaum [DaGr62].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos224.lean"]
theorem erdos_224 {d : ℕ} (A : Finset (ℝ^d)) (hcard : A.card = 2 ^ d + 1) :
    ∃ x y z : ℝ^d, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ z ∈ A ∧
      x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ z ∧ y ≠ z ∧ ObtuseAt x y z := by
  sorry

end Erdos224

reformulations.difference: Uses a negative inner product instead of an explicit angle inequality. This includes straight angles, rather than imposing an additional angle < π condition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Gerencsér–Harangi §1 explicitly identifies the Erdős–Danzer–Grünbaum problem with the bound for sets whose angles are all at most π/2. Thus the required witness has angle strictly greater than π/2, including π. I proved in scratch.lean that ObtuseAt x y z ↔ Real.pi / 2 < EuclideanGeometry.angle y x z. For nonzero edges, the norm product is positive and the sign of the inner product gives precisely this angle inequality. Zero edges cannot satisfy ObtuseAt; moreover, its strict negativity implies all three points are distinct.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Some unsolved problems, Michigan Mathematical Journal 4 (1957), 291–300, §B, problem 19, p. 296: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1957-13.pdf
B. Gerencsér and V. Harangi, Acute sets of exponentially optimal size, arXiv:1709.03411v2, §1 (LaTeX source): https://arxiv.org/e-print/1709.03411v2

L. Danzer and B. Grünbaum, Über zwei Probleme bezüglich konvexer Körper von P. Erdös und von V. L. Klee, Math. Z. 79 (1962), 95–99: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01193107 (publisher's bibliographic page and references; full text unavailable)
Crossref bibliographic search for the cited Danzer–Grünbaum paper: https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=Uber%20zwei%20Probleme%20bezuglich%20konvexer%20Korper%20Danzer%20Grunbaum&rows=3
Rényi Institute bibliography of Erdős's papers: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html
review.notes: Both declarations are faithful to the mathematical problem. Erdős's original 1957 problem 19 states the exact 2^d+1 threshold. Scratch proofs check repeated points, obtuse/right/acute/straight examples, the harmless d=0 extension (no eligible set exists), and satisfiability of the cardinality hypothesis in every positive dimension. I also proved equivalence between the exact threshold and the standard non-obtuse-set cardinality bound. The solved status agrees with the 2017 literature's attribution to Danzer–Grünbaum (1962). The linked external proof states precisely the repository claim; after three proof-only adaptations from its advertised Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1 to the installed version, it compiled with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], without sorryAx. All experiments are under /workspace/review/. Access limitation: erdosproblems.com/224 returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive user agents, and the 1962 article's full text was unavailable; the posed claim was independently checked against Erdős's original paper and the explicit 2017 account.
